text: I’ve been going to Vegas pretty much my whole life, the under-21 version of it. So I’ve sat through a lot of shows before I could even gamble. Le Rêve at Wynn, we finally saw that one, and honestly it’s mixed, maybe worse than mixed. The good is the circular stage is genuinely smart. You look down into it, so from any seat you get a good view, and its a rare thing in Vegas. Some acts are good, strength stuff, aerialists, divers, all the good stuff. They are athletes, no question. But it reminds me of Cirque du Soleil, just not in a rip-off way, just that you see comparable feats done with maybe more clarity. But clarity is the problem. I still dont know what’s the story is about? Dream? Guy? Water? Its pretty images thrown at you with no real idea of what it was trying to tell. And its just too much going on. Too many things, too many people, too many wow moments on top of each other. More restraint would be nice. This is just more is better, stereotypical Vegas spectacle, so they crammed all in, and more is better, but not for us. Ticket: staying Wynn or Encore, they have deal where instead of 125 for the show you pay 99, that’s a good deal. Would I see it again, probably not, and pay again, no. Apart from a few stunts it was average, not blown away. I think nobody was. Some friends of mine liked it, so if you’ve not seen it, it’s probably worth a watch, just don’t expect to leave overwhelmed.
